story.originalTitle: Lando Norris reveals other 'opportunities' before signing new McLaren contract ahead of Italian Grand Prix
story.summaryEn: Lando Norris has revealed he had other opportunities before signing a new contract keeping him at McLaren until the end of 2030. Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle interviewed him ahead of the Italian Grand Prix about the deal and the title race.
detailZh: 兰多·诺里斯透露，在意大利大奖赛前与迈凯伦签署新合同之前，曾有过其他'机会'。
天空体育F1的马丁·布伦德尔采访了兰多·诺里斯，谈论他的新迈凯伦合同以及总冠军争夺战，这次采访将在本周末播出；请在天空体育F1观看意大利大奖赛周五练习赛，直播时间为上午11点30分和下午3点。
观看兰多·诺里斯迄今为止跌宕起伏的赛季，其中出现了多次退赛和多场分站冠军，使他处于争夺总冠军的行列之中。
兰多·诺里斯透露，在签署新合同留在迈凯伦至少到2030年底之前，他还有其他的机会。
诺里斯已经赢下了最近两场一级方程式比赛，自2019年首次亮相F1以来一直效力迈凯伦。他表示这份合同“可能是我签过的最容易下的决定”。
不过，这位26岁的车手在接受天空体育F1主持人马丁·布伦德尔将于本周末意大利大奖赛期间播出的广泛访谈中承认，确实还有其他选择。

“当然有机会。但那是一种积极的机会。有时候，机会是需要去赌一把的，”他说。
“就我个人而言，我是一个宁愿经历一两年艰难岁月，也不要立即取得成功的车手——就像几年前我在迈凯伦所做的那样。
“尽管我渴望每一年都能夺冠，但并不是所有事情都在于我明天就必须加入一支能在下一场比赛就获胜的车队，去做这个、做那个。”
伯尼·柯林斯在《The F1 Show》播客节目中表示，她认为兰多·诺里斯在最近连续两站获胜、状态提升之后，仍然处于总冠军争夺战之中。
诺里斯指出，迈凯伦拥有一支由车队领队扎克·布朗和安德烈亚·斯特拉率领的“强大”团队，这是他留在这支位于沃金的车队的一个关键原因。
他补充道：“其中很重要的一部分也是我开不开心？即使在我们没有赢的时候，我也很乐意留在迈凯伦，因为我依然拥有一个绝佳的机会，依然能做我热爱的工作，四处旅行并做所有这些事情。所以对我来说，并非一切都关乎极致的表现。很重要而且很大的一部分是我身边的人。
“仅仅是因为我感觉自己像在家里一样，而且我很享受这一切。这几乎和说‘我必须留在一支能够保持竞争力并赢得总冠军的车队’具有同样的分量。”
克雷格·斯莱特讨论荷兰大奖赛之后最热门的话题，包括兰多·诺里斯是否仍有争夺总冠军的机会
诺里斯目前状态正佳，他在匈牙利和荷兰最近两场大奖赛中都拿下杆位并夺冠，将他与总冠军领跑者安东内利的积分差距缩小到83分。
本周日他还有一次好机会，因为安东内利由于超出引擎使用配额而受到发车处罚，将从队尾发车。
不过，迈凯伦仍将面临挑战，需要击败拉塞尔，以及法拉利的汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔，他们两人都换上了升级版发动机。
汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔在蒙扎将获得车迷（意大利铁杆车迷，即tifosi）的巨大支持，那里拥有最具标志性的颁奖台，俯瞰着主直道，赛后还会有数千名车迷聚集。
法拉利为在蒙扎举行的F1意大利大奖赛发布了特别版涂装，向迈克尔·舒马赫致敬。
布伦德尔指出，汉密尔顿此前曾表示，在实现加入法拉利的“梦想”之前，他会留在梅赛德斯，并询问诺里斯将来是否会考虑加入这支车队。
这位迈凯伦车手说：“这不是我现在想考虑的事情。从小时候起，你总会想象自己处在不同的位置。”
“我的梦想一直是留在迈凯伦。这就是为什么我觉得自己现在处在一个非常幸运的位置。但你总想体验另一边的情况，无论是法拉利、其他车队，还是梅赛德斯。”
“这就是人性。我认为你会想去体验处于这个位置和那个位置是什么感觉。”
兰多·诺里斯与天空体育的罗布·琼斯坐下来，畅谈他与迈凯伦签下多年续约合同、延长留队时间的事宜
"另外，还有其他车队的历史。刘易斯当年也是从迈凯伦去了梅赛德斯，然后又去了法拉利，我觉得尝试不同的东西、体验不同的经历其实也挺酷的。"
“目前，我会说我没有去想这件事。但请在2030年底再问我一次。”

detailEn: Lando Norris reveals other 'opportunities' before signing new McLaren contract ahead of Italian Grand Prix

Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle caught up with Lando Norris to discuss his new McLaren contract and the title race in an interview that will air this weekend; watch Friday's practice sessions for the Italian GP at 11.30am and 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1
Watch Lando Norris' roller-coaster season so far, which has seen several DNFs and race wins, putting him in the mix to challenge for the title
Lando Norris has revealed he had other opportunities before signing a new contract to stay at McLaren until at least the end of 2030.
Norris, who has won the last two Formula 1 races, has been with McLaren since making his F1 debut in 2019 and says the contract was "probably the easiest contract I've had to sign".
The 26-year-old admitted though, in a wide-ranging interview with Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle which will air at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, that there were other options.

"There was opportunity of course. But opportunity that is positive. There's opportunities to gamble at times," he said.
"I'm a driver that personally I would take one or two tougher years over instant success - as I did a few years ago with McLaren.
"As much as I want to win every single year, not everything is about I need to be with a team tomorrow that's going to win the next race and do this and do that."
Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Lando Norris is still in the title fight after his recent improvement with two back-to-back wins
Norris pointed to the "strong" group of people at McLaren, led by team bosses Zak Brown and Andrea Stella, as a key reason to stay at the Woking-based outfit.

He added: "A good amount of it is also am I just happy? I was happy to be with McLaren even when we weren't winning because I'm still in an amazing opportunity and I still get to do the job I love and travel and do all these things. So not everything to me is about ultimate performance. A lot of it and a big part of it is the people that I'm with.
"Just the fact I feel I'm at home and I'm enjoying it. And that almost has enough control as saying 'I need to be with a team that is going to be performing and winning championships'."
Craig Slater discusses the biggest talking points off the back of the Dutch Grand Prix, including if the championship chase is still on for Lando Norris

Norris is currently in great form after claiming pole position and the win at the last two Grands Prix in Hungary and the Netherlands to cut his deficit to championship leader Kimi Antonelli to 83 points.
He has another good opportunity this Sunday as Antonelli will start at the back of the field due to grid penalties for exceeding his engine allocation.
But, McLaren will still have the challenge of beating George Russell plus Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, who both have upgraded engines.
Hamilton and Leclerc will have huge support from the Tifosi at Monza, which features the most iconic podium as it overlooks the main straight and thousands of fans post-race.
Ferrari has unveiled its one-off livery, paying tribute to Michael Schumacher, for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix at Monza.

Brundle pointed out Hamilton had previously stated he would stay at Mercedes before achieving his "dream" of joining Ferrari and asked if Norris would ever consider joining the Scuderia in the future.
The McLaren driver said: "That's not something I want to think about for now. Since I was a kid, you always think of yourself in different positions.

"My dream was always to be with McLaren. That's why I feel like I'm in a very fortunate position as I am. But you always want to experience the other side of things, whether that is Ferrari or other teams and Mercedes.
"It's just human. I think that you want to experience what it's like to be in this position and that position.
Lando Norris sits down with Sky Sports' Rob Jones to discuss extending his stay with McLaren in a multi-year contract extension

"Also, the history of other teams. The fact Lewis also went to Mercedes from McLaren and then to Ferrari, I think it's also pretty cool that you try different things and you experience different stuff.
"For now, I'll say I'm not thinking of it. But ask me again at the end of 2030."

detailEn: Mexico City GP: Lando Norris pips Kimi Antonelli in final practice to set up thrilling Mexico qualifying

Lando Norris and Kimi Antonelli were separated by just 0.001s at the top of the timesheet in final practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix; watch qualifying later at 9pm with Sunday's race at 8pm (build-up from 6.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1

Sky Sports F1's David Croft and Karun Chandok discuss Esteban Ocon being replaced by Haas for the Mexico City GP, Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen being handed a grid penalty for their P2 collision and Isack Hajar's paddock altercation with a fan
McLaren's Lando Norris pipped Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 0.001s in final practice for the Mexico City Grand Prix to set up a thrilling qualifying.
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc had topped both of Friday's practice sessions but McLaren and Mercedes showed their hand to outpace the Monegasque driver by one tenth of a second.
Antonelli is likely to become world champion in Sunday's race as he only needs a top-nine finish to secure the Formula 1 drivers' title.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was fourth while Red Bull appear to be out of the pole position battle as Max Verstappen was 0.351s off the pace, but there seems to be a genuine three-team fight at the front for qualifying later on Saturday at 9pm (build-up from 8pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Regardless of what he does in qualifying, Verstappen cannot start on pole position as he and Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson have a one-grid place penalty for colliding in second practice on Friday.
The stewards called the incident "unacceptable", with both drivers admitting the clash was "unnecessary and clumsy".
Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and Red Bull's Max Verstappen make contact during FP2 at the Mexico City GP - the clash would eventually lead to both drivers receiving a grid penalty
More drama took place before final practice on Saturday as Haas made the shock decision to replace Esteban Ocon with reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the remainder of the weekend.
The team provided no reason for replacing Ocon, but confirmed the Frenchman was not suffering from illness.
Haas recently confirmed that Ocon will be leaving the team at the end of this season after two years with the American-owned squad, with Brazilian youngster Rafael Camara signed as his replacement.
Hirakwa, a 24 Hours of Le Mans winner, has taken part in several practice sessions for Haas over the last two years and was 19th in final practice, six tenths down on team-mate Oliver Bearman.

车队未说明换下奥康的原因，但确认这位法国车手并非患病。

这位法国车手在被赛事工程师劳拉·穆勒告知其驾驶计划有变后，恳求道“别这样对我”。
哈斯车队最近确认，奥康将在本赛季结束后离开这支美国所有的车队，他已在队效力两年。
车队声明写道：“TGR哈斯F1车队储备车手平川亮将在本周末墨西哥城大奖赛的剩余赛程中替换埃斯特班·奥康，时间为10月31日星期六至11月1日星期日。”
“平川亮（32岁）曾随丰田GAZOO Racing两度赢得国际汽联世界耐力锦标赛冠军（2022年、2023年），并夺得勒芒24小时耐力赛冠军（2022年）。他于10月30日星期五在罗德里格斯兄弟赛道参加了第一节自由练习，这是他本赛季第三次驾驶VF-26赛车出战自由练习，最终位列全场第15名。”
“这位日本车手将在星期六的第三节自由练习和排位赛以及星期日的71圈大奖赛中与队友奥利·贝尔曼搭档——这将是平川亮的F1正赛首秀。”

detailEn: Esteban Ocon: Haas replace French driver with Ryo Hirakawa for remainder of Mexico City GP weekend without providing reason

Esteban Ocon will take no further part in the Mexico City GP, with Haas replacing French driver with Ryo Hirakawa; Haas gave no reason for Ocon's replacement; Ocon is leaving the team at the end of the season
Esteban Ocon has been replaced by Ryo Hirakawa at Haas for the remainder of the Mexico City Grand Prix.
The team provided no reason for replacing Ocon, but confirmed the Frenchman was not suffering from illness.

Ocon vented his frustrations on the team radio while finishing 13th following second practice and will take no further part in the race as Hirakawa will take his place on the grid at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodríguez.
Ocon questioned the team's decision to run him on the medium rather than soft tyre during second practice on Friday.
The Frenchman pleaded "don't do this to me" to his race engineer Laura Mueller after being informed of a change to his run-plan.
Haas recently confirmed that Ocon will be leaving the team at the end of this season after two years with the American-owned squad.
A team statement read: "TGR Haas F1 Team reserve driver Ryō Hirakawa will replace Esteban Ocon for the remainder of the weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix, Saturday 31 October - Sunday 1 November.

"Hirakawa (32), a two-time winner of the FIA World Endurance Championship (2022, 2023) and 24 Hours of Le Mans Winner (2022) with Toyota GAZOO Racing, participated in FP1 at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Friday 30 October - his third free practice outing of the season driving the VF-26, finishing 15th overall.
"The Japanese driver will partner teammate Ollie Bearman through final practice and qualifying on Saturday and Sunday's 71-lap grand prix - Hirakawa's Formula 1 race debut."
